svg.text: Connecting Training Engineering to Inference Engineering
AI Training Engineering (This Course)
• Goal: Learn optimal weights from massive datasets
• Memory footprint: 16 bytes/param (128.5 GB) + saved activations
• Compute profile: 6ND FLOPs (forward + backward) or 8ND (recompute)
• Hardware topology: 256 to 16,384 GPUs, NVLink + InfiniBand NDR
• Primary metric: Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU), target ≥ 40%
• State lifetime: Static weights + optimizer state held for entire run
• Bottlenecks: HBM capacity (OOM), inter-node collective bandwidth
• Execution units: Micro-batches, gradient accumulation, global step
AI Inference Engineering (Companion Course)
• Goal: Serve trained weights to streaming users cheaply & reliably
• Memory footprint: 2 bytes/param (16 GB) + dynamic KV cache
• Compute profile: 2N FLOPs prefill; memory bandwidth bound decode
• Hardware topology: 1 to 8 GPUs per replica, autoscaled pool
• Primary metric: Latency percentiles (p95 TTFT ≤ 500 ms, TPOT ≤ 25 ms)
• State lifetime: Ephemeral KV cache created and destroyed per request
• Bottlenecks: Memory bandwidth (decode), KV cache capacity
• Execution units: Paged attention blocks, continuous batching
How Training Decisions Dictate Production Serving Costs
• Grouped-Query Attention (GQA): 8 KV heads vs 32 query heads cuts serving KV cache by 4× (128 KiB vs 512 KiB per token).
• Vocabulary Size: 128,256 BPE vocabulary compresses sequences, cutting inference decode steps at the cost of embedding memory.
• Chinchilla Overtraining: Training 8B past 20 tok/param to 15T tokens spends training compute to lower perpetual serving cost.
